sourcingPolicy: Permitted public government guidance, licensed open-access guidance and targeted society-guideline factual checks. Independent original synthesis and fictional observations. Source prose, excerpts, tables, figures and algorithms are excluded.

evidenceClaims.statement: Initial nonoperative treatment and laparoscopic surgery both have guideline support for selected appendiceal abscess presentations.
evidenceClaims.limitation: WSES recommendations 6.1-6.2 condition the approach on expertise and setting. SAGES KQ3 conditionally favors surgery while identifying a discrete abscess and significant cecal inflammation as reasons to consider initial nonoperative care. A universal comparative key is withheld.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Stable patients with a primary appendiceal abscess or phlegmon.

evidenceClaims.statement: The verified guidelines differ on routine interval appendectomy after successful nonoperative treatment in an asymptomatic younger adult.
evidenceClaims.limitation: WSES 2020 recommendation 6.3 advises against routine interval appendectomy in patients younger than 40, reserving it for recurrence. SAGES 2024 KQ8 conditionally favors interval appendectomy in adults. The newer WSES full recommendation needs permitted verification. No general younger-adult item is keyed.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Asymptomatic younger adults after successful nonoperative management of appendiceal abscess or phlegmon.

evidenceClaims.statement: Management of appendiceal NETs measuring 1-2 cm requires a more individualized assessment than the larger-tumor resection rule.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One directly verified current specialty guideline describes controversy and consideration of pathology, patient factors and multidisciplinary review. A mandatory colectomy rule based on one intermediate-size adverse feature is withheld.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with an appendiceal NET measuring 1-2 cm.

evidenceClaims.statement: Definitively treated uncomplicated appendicitis generally requires no postoperative therapeutic antibiotic course.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Supports a ranked future gap. The directly verified guidelines share authors and evidence. A sufficiently discriminating new operative-classification question remains to be authored, with the newer guideline checked before exact duration rules are used.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Patients after definitive appendectomy for uncomplicated appendicitis.

evidenceClaims.statement: MRI can follow inconclusive ultrasound when appendicitis remains suspected during pregnancy.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One directly verified guideline, recommendation 1.13.2, supports the relationship. This is a ranked scope gap with no keyed new pregnancy item. Current population-specific guidance and a consequential close alternative require further permitted verification.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Pregnant patients with suspected appendicitis after inconclusive ultrasound.

evidenceClaims.statement: Appendectomy is sufficient surgical treatment for a margin-negative LAMN with an intact wall and no peritoneal involvement.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One directly verified current specialty guideline, recommendation 12. Used for counterfactuals and the boundary against invasive carcinoma. Surveillance details remain outside the scored task.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Completely resected, nonperforated LAMN without peritoneal disease.

evidenceClaims.statement: A subcentimeter appendiceal NET without unfavorable features can be treated by appendectomy that includes the mesoappendix.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One directly verified current specialty guideline, recommendation 7. Used as a counterfactual boundary. This packet supplies no universal rule for 1-2-cm tumors or a surveillance schedule.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: A completely removed appendiceal NET smaller than 1 cm with favorable histology.

evidenceClaims.statement: Progressive or persistent right-sided abdominal pain after negative imaging can warrant exploratory laparoscopy for appendicitis or another cause.
evidenceClaims.limitation: WSES recommendation 1.12 directly supports exploration after a progressive clinical course. NIDDK corroborates surgery for ongoing symptoms only at a general level. An adequate negative examination initially supports observation. The 2025 WSES exact update was unavailable for permitted full-text verification.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults with unresolved right iliac fossa symptoms after cross-sectional evaluation and serial assessment.

evidenceClaims.statement: CT can resolve persistent diagnostic uncertainty after nondiagnostic ultrasound in a stable nonpregnant adult with suspected appendicitis.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Used to audit the old modality questions. MRI is also definitive. The legacy availability sentence does much of their discriminating work.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Stable nonpregnant adults with uncertain appendicitis.

evidenceClaims.statement: An appendicolith makes an antibiotics-first appendicitis course less favorable and strengthens the case for appendectomy.
evidenceClaims.limitation: A treatment-risk modifier within shared clinical decisions. No universal prohibition, exact failure probability or uniquely required treatment for every patient is asserted. Used for the legacy audit.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults considering nonoperative treatment of imaging-confirmed appendicitis.

evidenceClaims.statement: An older adult recovering from an appendiceal abscess warrants evaluation for an underlying appendiceal or colonic neoplasm.
evidenceClaims.limitation: The drafted patient is 62 with a persistent focal appendiceal abnormality. No age threshold or mandatory policy for all younger adults is keyed. The publications differ on routine interval appendectomy.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults after nonoperative treatment of complicated appendicitis, especially older patients or those with suspicious interval imaging.

evidenceClaims.statement: Suspected appendiceal neoplasia calls for colonoscopy to assess synchronous colonic disease before formal resection planning.
evidenceClaims.limitation: ASCRS recommendation 1 is the direct current guideline. WSES independently supports colonic screening in the post-abscess older-adult context. Neither establishes colonoscopy as a complete histologic examination of the appendix.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Patients with suspected appendiceal tumors, including an older adult with a persistent post-abscess appendiceal nodule.

evidenceClaims.statement: Interval appendectomy is favored after complicated appendicitis in an older adult with persistent imaging suspicion for appendiceal neoplasia.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Conditional guidance. The case has resolved infection, a focal residual nodule and a free appendiceal base. Normal cecal mucosa does not supply histology of that mural nodule. Exact timing and a universal younger-adult rule are withheld.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: An older adult after successful nonoperative treatment of appendiceal abscess with a suspicious persistent lesion.

evidenceClaims.statement: An abnormal appendix encountered incidentally can be removed intact with a grossly clear base, preserving definitive specimen assessment before deciding on oncologic colectomy.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One directly verified current specialty guideline, recommendation 2. The base and extent govern resection. Suspected mucinous lesions require avoidance of rupture. No automatic operation is specified for extensive peritoneal disease.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: An incidentally dilated, unruptured appendix with a separable uninvolved base and no peritoneal deposits.

evidenceClaims.statement: A microscopic positive margin in an otherwise completely removed, nonperforated LAMN does not automatically require further resection.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One directly verified current specialty guideline. The underlying data are limited. This proposal requires exact pathology, absence of gross residual disease, no perforation and no peritoneal mucin. Melissa must review observation against local re-excision. Surveillance intensity is left open.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Completely excised nonperforated low-grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasm with microscopic margin involvement and no peritoneal disease.

evidenceClaims.statement: Infiltrative malignant glands distinguish appendiceal adenocarcinoma from a noninfiltrative low-grade mucinous neoplasm.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One directly verified current specialty guideline. A fully evaluated permanent specimen is supplied in the draft. A small biopsy or uncertain frozen section would not establish the same extent.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Permanent pathology assessment of an appendectomy specimen.

evidenceClaims.statement: Nonmetastatic appendiceal adenocarcinoma generally warrants oncologic right hemicolectomy with regional nodal assessment.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One directly verified current specialty guideline, recommendation 13. The draft has invasion into mesoappendiceal fat, adequate staging and a fit patient. The recommendation is not generalized to isolated LAMN or disseminated peritoneal disease.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Fit adults with invasive appendiceal adenocarcinoma and no distant or peritoneal metastases.

evidenceClaims.statement: Infiltrative appendiceal goblet-cell epithelial tumors follow an adenocarcinoma treatment pathway despite possible focal neuroendocrine-marker expression.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One directly verified current specialty guideline. The exact diagnosis is confirmed on expert permanent review. A stain result by itself is insufficient to reclassify the tumor.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Localized appendiceal goblet cell adenocarcinoma.

evidenceClaims.statement: Somatostatin-receptor PET/CT can clarify staging of a well-differentiated appendiceal NET when cross-sectional imaging leaves possible metastases unresolved.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One directly verified current specialty guideline, recommendation 5. Ga-DOTA PET/CT is favored over older receptor scintigraphy for sensitivity and over FDG PET/CT in well-differentiated NETs. Exact comparative performance estimates are excluded.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Patients with appendiceal NETs larger than 2 cm or indeterminate metastatic findings.

evidenceClaims.statement: For a nonmetastatic appendiceal NET larger than 2 cm, right hemicolectomy addresses the regional nodal basin even after a margin-negative appendectomy.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One directly verified current specialty guideline, recommendation 7. The exact greater-than-2-cm threshold is directly stated there. Management of tumors measuring 1-2 cm is withheld as a disputed boundary.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: A fit adult with a 2.6-cm well-differentiated appendiceal NET and no distant disease.

evidenceClaims.statement: Selected patients with appendiceal mucinous neoplasia and peritoneal dissemination merit peritoneal-surface surgical assessment for cytoreduction and intraperitoneal treatment.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One directly verified current specialty guideline, recommendations 13-15. Right colectomy does not by itself address diffuse peritoneal disease. Systemic chemotherapy has limited activity in low-grade disease. Referral does not assert that every patient is operable or requires one HIPEC regimen.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: A fit patient with biopsy-confirmed low-grade appendiceal mucinous peritoneal disease and no distant solid-organ metastases.

evidenceClaims.statement: Intravenous contrast-enhanced CT helps localize an intra-abdominal infectious source and plan source control in a stable postoperative adult.
evidenceClaims.limitation: The publications overlap in authorship and underlying evidence. Clinical recovery followed by renewed deep abdominal symptoms is constructed patient data. CT is compared with focused superficial ultrasound and abdominal radiographs, not with an equally comprehensive appropriate alternative.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: A stable adult with suspected intra-abdominal infection after appendectomy.

evidenceClaims.statement: A localized postoperative abscess without generalized peritonitis can be treated with image-guided catheter drainage and antibiotics when the collection has a safe access route.
evidenceClaims.limitation: WSES statement 30 and Global Alliance source-control guidance directly support this pathway. Their evidence overlaps. No abscess-size cutoff or universal superiority over operative drainage is claimed. The case supplies a single accessible collection and persistent infection despite antibiotics.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: A stable adult after appendectomy with a persistent accessible pelvic abscess and no demonstrated ongoing enteric leak.

evidenceClaims.statement: Generalized postoperative peritonitis or uncontrolled enteric leakage requires prompt operative source control.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Used as the decision-changing counterfactual to localized percutaneous drainage. Operation and route depend on physiology and anatomy. Resuscitation and antibiotics are shared background care.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Postoperative patients with uncontrolled contamination or generalized peritonitis.

evidenceClaims.statement: After adequate source control and clinical recovery, a completed short antibiotic course need not be extended until every inflammatory laboratory result normalizes.
evidenceClaims.limitation: The patient has already completed four days after drainage. Global Alliance statement 8 directly supports this completed-course scenario and compares fixed treatment with physiologic-normalization endpoints. This item does not ask for a minimum duration or override a shorter current appendicitis protocol. Exact new WSES duration requires a permitted full-text check. Persistent illness would change the task to renewed source assessment.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: An immunocompetent adult with a drained appendectomy-associated abscess, clinical recovery and a falling mildly elevated leukocyte count.

evidenceClaims.statement: A limited appendiceal tissue sample does not establish the final classification of the unsampled lesion; permanent assessment of the complete resection specimen informs candidacy for regional oncologic resection.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Targeted check of ASCRS 2025 recommendation 2 and epithelial classification. The fictional specimen map demonstrates a separate infiltrative focus; no probability of sampling error is asserted. One adequate directly verified guideline.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Appendiceal neoplasm after a limited outside review and complete permanent specimen review.

evidenceClaims.statement: A permanent biopsy containing low-grade mucinous epithelium in a deposit outside the appendix establishes cellular extra-appendiceal disease in that sampled site; an acellular sample from another site does not negate it.
evidenceClaims.limitation: ASCRS 2025 recommendations 2, 11 and 14 support representative biopsy, tissue-based cellularity and limitations of cytology. The conclusion is confined to represented tissue, not a claim that all deposits share that grade or that cytology should be routinely ordered.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Separately labelled mucin and solid-nodule samples obtained at appendectomy.

evidenceClaims.statement: A liver lesion with homogeneous fluid signal, a thin smooth wall and no enhancing internal tissue on adequate contrast MRI has the characteristic morphology of a simple hepatic cyst.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Publisher full text and CC BY 4.0 verified. This is a narrow morphology claim, not a claim that a negative receptor scan excludes all liver metastases. Imaging must actually resolve the represented lesions.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adequate precontrast, fluid-sensitive and postcontrast liver MRI of previously indeterminate lesions.

evidenceClaims.statement: A CT interpretation is limited to the images actually reviewed; an export missing already acquired images differs from an unperformed acquisition.
evidenceClaims.limitation: The source supports contrast CT for source localization. Retrieval versus repeat acquisition is the logical consequence of this fictional acquisition and transfer log, not a guideline-tested procedure ranking. The archive confirms the complete current acquisition and immediate review access; a changing clinical state or inadequate source images would invalidate the retrieval key.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Stable postoperative adult whose initial report used a subset of the current CT acquisition.

withheldDisagreements.teachingPoint: Verified guidance supports selected use of both approaches and conditions recommendations on expertise, anatomy and inflammatory burden. A universal comparative key is withheld.
WSES 2020 and SAGES 2024 give different routine policies. The newer WSES full recommendation remains unverified under permitted access.

withheldDisagreements.reason: The permitted guideline reviews limited data against routine additional treatment, but the exact viable-epithelium margin comparison does not establish observation as uniquely preferable to local cecal re-excision. The reviewer explicitly requests Melissa's judgment. No fair single best key is asserted.
withheldDisagreements.nextAction: Should observation be the uniquely preferred reoperation decision over local cecal re-excision for these exact facts? State the evidence and limits that settle that comparison, or keep it unscored.

withheldDisagreements.reason: The tracer choice remains basic recall when functional imaging is prespecified. A broader next-investigation comparison needs a directly supported hierarchy versus dedicated liver MRI; the verified guideline supports NET-specific imaging without resolving that exact sequence. No accepted basic-purpose exception exists.
withheldDisagreements.nextAction: Define the exact acquisition limitation and staging goal that make one next investigation preferable, with direct support. Otherwise retain this as an unkeyed planning slot rather than imply either study completes staging.
